clue.text: Finishes without century and is defeated

indicators.note: without tells us the century letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: finishes means closes, as a shop closes for the day
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A batsman finishes his innings short of a hundred and his side goes down.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose a game is to be beaten in it, so the verb in the third person matches 'is defeated'.

clue.text: See 23
Cocaine dealer possibly a lecturer in online talk describing some mountain-tops

parts.note: snow is slang for cocaine, so a man selling it might jokingly be a snowman

indicators.note: in places the lecturer's letter inside the online talk

parts.note: a TED talk is a lecture posted online
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A drug dealer, maybe an academic, gives an internet lecture about peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaks covered by a blanket of white in winter are described as snow-clad in this way.

clue.text: Various students turn up not serving alcohol

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue means the letters for students are read upwards

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK
a dry bar or event serves no alcohol

explanation.surface: Assorted students show up at a party with no booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a miscellaneous assortment, as in 'sundry items' meaning several mixed things.

clue.text: Scottish party take note of some work by composer

parts.note: Alba is a Scottish independence party founded by Alex Salmond
NB, nota bene, is Latin for 'take note'
an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A Scottish political group pays attention to a piece by some composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg wrote the operas Wozzeck and Lulu, so he is a named example of a composer.

clue.text: Sailor backed proposal to cut energy and ran off

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: to cut says the letter for energy is removed from the word for backing a motion

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it, so seconded means backed a proposal
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sailor who supported a motion to slash energy then fled.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to leave secretly, usually to escape the law, which is running off.

clue.text: Turn strong women's organisation into group which bloviates

indicators.note: into says the turn, strong and women's pieces go inside the group

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians or people
a go is a turn in a game
F is forte, the musical marking for loud or strong
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

explanation.surface: Converting the Women's Institute into a talking shop full of pompous speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is 5-down plus 14-across. The WI is a British community organisation for women, known for jam and Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloviate is to talk at length pompously, and a windbag is a person who does exactly that.

clue.text: Lacking function, bodyguard is possible cat-killer

parts.note: no means lacking, as in 'no money'
sine is a trigonometric function
the SS began as Hitler's bodyguard unit

explanation.surface: An unemployed bodyguard turns out to be a cat-murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'curiosity killed the cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Curiosity killed the cat, and prying curiosity is the quality defined, so it could be the killer.

clue.text: Fish the Spanish stock online

indicators.note: stock is read as to hold within, so the Spanish article holds the online letter

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
E, as in email, is the prefix for online

explanation.surface: Spanish fishmongers sell their catch over the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snake-like fish, such as the European species eaten jellied in London.

clue.text: Pests with 7 fingers — horrible!

indicators.note: horrible suggests a nasty mess, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the answer to 7-down is the fish, EEL

explanation.surface: Slimy fish grabbed with bare fingers is a nasty sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids that suck sap from garden plants are a gardener's nuisance insects.

clue.text: Also called some bipartisan wonks back

indicators.note: back says the run of letters taken is read from right to left
some says only part of the words bipartisan wonks is used, a run straddling them

explanation.surface: Policy experts from both parties turn up again under another name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks SANWONK from 'bipartisan wonks', and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce an alias or alternative name, as in 'Cassius Clay, later going by Ali'.

clue.text: Ballet one to promote in Georgia

indicators.note: in says the other pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for Georgia

parts.note: GE is the country code for Georgia
I is the Roman numeral one
to promote a product is to sell it

explanation.surface: A ballet company is out to market itself in Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Giselle is Adolphe Adam's Romantic ballet of 1841, a classic of the repertoire.

clue.text: Ballerina not many forget dancing

indicators.note: dancing suggests letters moving about, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hardly anyone forgets a great ballerina in action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges the thirteen letters of 'not many forget'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Margot Fonteyn was the Royal Ballet's prima ballerina, partnered famously by Nureyev.

clue.text: Key primate's farewell protects against potential release of pressure

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
an ape is a primate

indicators.note: protects says the farewell word wraps around the letter for against

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
V, versus, means against

explanation.surface: A crucial ape's goodbye keeps it safe from harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A valve that opens when a boiler builds up too much steam lets the excess out, as a safety outlet.

clue.text: Southwestern research station lists cakes

parts.note: the ISS is the International Space Station, an orbiting research lab
rolls are lists of names, as in electoral rolls

explanation.surface: A research base in the southwest keeps inventories of baked goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge rolled up around jam is a classic British teatime sponge confection.

clue.text: See 5
Parachutes, I see, regularly fail, having excess fluid

parts.note: to parachute supplies is to drop them, so parachutes means drops
C is the letter that sounds like 'see', as in text-speak 'I c'

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of fail is taken

explanation.surface: A skydiver's parachutes keep failing, which is concerning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the alternate letters A and L from 'fail'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is an old name for oedema, the build-up of water in the body, and this adjective describes a sufferer.

clue.text: Blocks podcast Curt's boss uploaded

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
loaded, read as held within a cargo, says the letters sit inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Curt's manager puts a podcast online.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'uploaded' into 'up' and 'loaded': 'loaded' hides STCURTSBO in 'podcast Curt's boss', and 'up' reads it upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for getting in the way, as debris impedes a road.

clue.text: M*A*S*H actor featured in fashionable Ur (as it was)

indicators.note: featured in says the actor appears inside the word for fashionable

parts.note: chic means stylish or fashionable
Alan Alda starred as Hawkeye in the TV series M*A*S*H

explanation.surface: A TV actor appears in a stylish ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur was the Mesopotamian city called 'Ur of the Chaldees' in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient city lay in Chaldea, so in its day it was a Chaldean place; the adjective names that region.

clue.text: See 25
Set pieces oddly missing fencing kit

indicators.note: oddly missing says the odd-numbered letters of set pieces go, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Planned plays in a match lack some of the gear for fencing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly missing' drops the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of SETPIECES, leaving E, P, E, E.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is one of the three swords used in sport fencing, so it is part of a fencer's equipment.

clue.text: Mint with pretty flowers seems to develop last of all

indicators.note: last of all says the final letter of every one of the words before it is taken

explanation.surface: A mint plant with lovely blooms appears to grow late.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic herb of the Lamiaceae family, the botanical family of mint.

clue.text: Dancer found rule very silly

indicators.note: silly suggests the words are muddled up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer discovered that a regulation was ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges the thirteen letters of 'found rule very'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was the Soviet-born star who defected and became the leading male ballet performer of his era.

clue.text: Starting now, understanding the German has less on

indicators.note: Starting says the opening letters of now and understanding are taken

parts.note: der is German for 'the'

explanation.surface: From this moment, the German grasps that he wears fewer clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone more naked than another is wearing fewer clothes, the comparative of bare.

clue.text: Ballet to satisfy one's appetite with disappointingly feeble content

indicators.note: content is read as contents, so the feeble word sits inside the word for satisfying

parts.note: to slake is to satisfy a thirst or craving
wan means pale and weak, as in a wan smile

explanation.surface: Eating your fill but with a meagre, unsatisfying filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's best-known ballet, about the swan princess Odette.

clue.text: Very funny fat early protestant

parts.note: LOL, laugh out loud, is text-speak for something very funny
lard is pig fat used in cooking

explanation.surface: A hilariously overweight churchman from the early Reformation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe in the 14th century, forerunners of the Reformation.

clue.text: Ballet smaller, certainly, keeping record concealed

parts.note: less means smaller in amount

indicators.note: keeping says the word for certainly holds the record and concealed pieces

parts.note: yes means certainly
an LP is a long-playing record
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A smaller ballet company, surely, kept a recording hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Sylphides is Fokine's one-act ballet set to Chopin, about woodland spirits.

clue.text: About to reverse country's precedent

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about with dates

indicators.note: to reverse says the country's name is written backwards

parts.note: Wales is a country of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A nation is about to overturn a ruling that set a legal pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Law built from earlier judges' decisions is the body of judicial precedent.

clue.text: Parts of Windows allow Spooner to store weapons

indicators.note: Spooner names Rev. William Spooner, famed for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: to cache is to hide away in store
swords are bladed weapons

explanation.surface: Permitting a famous clergyman to stockpile arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allow Spooner to' swaps the opening sounds of CACHE SWORDS, giving the 'k' sound to the second word and the 's' to the first.
explanation.definitionFit: In a sliding sash window, cords over pulleys carry the counterweights, so they are components of such windows.

clue.text: Father near missing the start of hymn of praise

parts.note: Pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: missing the start says the first letter of the word for near is dropped

parts.note: near can mean stingy, the same as mean

explanation.surface: A dad close by but without the opening of the hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' here is the old sense of tight-fisted, i.e. MEAN; 'missing the start' removes its M.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean is a song or chant of praise or triumph, originally to Apollo.
